# Introduction

State the problem and why it is open. Cite prior work in brackets
[@shannon1948] or in running text, as @knuth1984 argued for programs
written to be read. The bibliography lives in `references.bib` and the
reference list at the end is generated.

# Method

Numbered equations get a label and can be referenced (@eq-throughput):

$$
T = \frac{N_{\mathrm{bytes}}}{t_{\mathrm{end}} - t_{\mathrm{start}}}
$$ {#eq-throughput}

Code and commands go in fenced blocks:

```sh
python scripts/make_figures.py   # data/*.csv -> figures/*.svg
```

# Results

@fig-results is plotted from `data/results.csv` on every build, so new data
reaches the PDF by replacing the CSV. @tbl-results gives the same numbers
at two block sizes.

![Throughput vs. block size.](figures/results.svg){#fig-results width=60% fig-alt="Line chart of throughput versus block size from 4 to 256 KiB; Method A rises from 120 to 655 MB/s and stays above Method B, which rises from 95 to 540 MB/s."}

| Block size | Method A (MB/s) | Method B (MB/s) |
|-----------:|----------------:|----------------:|
| 4 KiB | 120 | 95 |
| 256 KiB | 655 | 540 |

: Throughput at the smallest and largest block sizes {#tbl-results}
